action_items: Ari Kaplan: Send pricing sheet and cost scenarios by 2026-03-31

summary: Discovery focused on per-token economics and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Security and VPC requirements discussed; next step pilot + technical deep dive.
transcript_body:
Meeting header: 2026-03-29 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Ari Kaplan (Redwood AE), Samira Chen (Redwood SE), Tom Nguyen (CTO - Meridian), Priya Shah (Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (DevOps), Sasha (Analyst)

[00:00] Ari Kaplan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros — I'm Ari, AE at Redwood, and Samira is our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Tom Nguyen: Thanks Ari. I'm Tom, CTO at Meridian. We'll jump right in — budget constraints upfront: we have a hard cap for Q2 on inference costs, and we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:22] Ari Kaplan: Totally — that's exactly why we wanted to talk economics first. Curious: do you have any existing per-token spend targets or an expected token volume?
[00:31] Priya Shah: We're starting with roughly 100k tokens/day for our retrieval-augmented generation assistant, spiking to 400k on event days. Target net cost is around $0.0009 per token end-to-end, which I know is aggressive.
[00:45] Samira Chen: Right. So quick framing: Redwood Hosted gives fastest time-to-value with per-token pricing and managed capacity. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and lower unit costs at volume; Private (VPC/on-prem) is for regulatory and residency needs but has higher ops and infra costs.
[01:02] Liam O'Connor: When you say per-token pricing on Hosted, is that identical to Dedicated? i.e., do you bill the same per-token or is there a seat/commit aspect?
[01:12] Ari Kaplan: Good question. Hosted is usage-based per-token. Dedicated is usually a reserved capacity contract — monthly commit for GPU hours we convert into effective per-token pricing in your estimate. So you often see lower per-token at steady, high throughput.
[01:28] Sasha (Analyst): Any concrete numbers to use for our finance model?
[01:31] Ari Kaplan: I'll share a pricing sheet but to ballpark: for a standard generation model on Hosted you might see $0.0006-$0.0012 per token depending on model size and context length. Dedicated can push that down 20-50% depending on commit and utilization.
[01:45] Priya Shah: That's a wide range. The big driver for us is cold-start and tail latency — we can't have big host latency spikes for our traders. How does batching and KV cache affect this cost figure?
[01:56] Samira Chen: Two levers: batching increases throughput and lowers per-token compute cost but can add latency. Redwood has intelligent continuous batching with latency SLO controls — you set max latency and batch windows. KV/prefix caching reduces repeated compute for similar prompts or session state — huge wins for chat flows. In practice, we've seen effective token-cost reductions of 30-60% with caching for stateful apps.
[02:17] Tom Nguyen: 30-60% — that's significant. How do you measure cache hit rates and what's realistic for us?
[02:22] Samira Chen: Hit rate depends on your session patterns. For Meridian's assistant, if many queries reuse similar contexts or system prompts, you could see 40-50% hit rates. We'll instrument that in the pilot. We'll need a sample traffic profile from Liam.
[02:36] Liam O'Connor: I'll pull sample logs — it's mostly short queries with repeated portfolio prompts during market hours.
[02:41] Priya Shah: Another factor is quantization/precision. Do you support INT8 or 4-bit profiles that materially reduce cost?
[02:47] Samira Chen: Yes, Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per-model/workload. Some models can run in 4-bit quant with negligible quality loss depending on generation length. That reduces GPU memory and can increase throughput per GPU which reduces per-token cost. We'll include model-specific recommendations in the follow-up.
[03:01] Sasha: Security question — we require KMS-managed keys and audit logs. Is that available on Hosted?
[03:06] Ari Kaplan: Hosted supports encrypted-at-rest and in-transit and has enterprise options for customer-managed keys and audit trails. For the strictest controls, Private (VPC or on-prem) gives full KMS/HSM integration and customer-controlled networking.
[03:19] Tom Nguyen: So tradeoffs are cost vs control. If our budget is tight, Dedicated might be the sweet spot?
[03:25] Samira Chen: Exactly. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and cost with lower unit economics for steady loads, while Private adds control but additional infra spend.
[03:33] Priya Shah: On modeling costs, can you give us a sample invoice simulation? We want token-level breakout and the impact of batching/caching/quantization.
[03:41] Ari Kaplan: We'll send a detailed cost scenario spreadsheet — we'll model 3 scenarios: Hosted baseline, Dedicated with 3-month commit, and Dedicated+KV caching with expected hit rates. Also show sensitivity to peak spikes.
[03:53] Tom Nguyen: For Dedicated, what's the commit sizing? Are we buying GPU nodes or tokens?
[03:58] Samira Chen: You commit to reserved capacity measured in GPU-hours or vGPU units. We map that to expected daily token throughput using model throughput curves. If utilization is higher than expected, you can always buy burst capacity.
[04:11] Liam O'Connor: How about autoscaling costs? Market hours see 10x traffic spike for an hour. Will commit cover that or do we pay overage?
[04:18] Ari Kaplan: Commit covers baseline. For spikes you can configure burst pools or fall back to Hosted; we can show economics of burst pricing versus pure overage. Many customers use Dedicated baseline + Hosted burst to avoid overcommitting.
[04:31] Priya Shah: Is there a minimum contract length for Dedicated?
[04:34] Ari Kaplan: Typical dedicated commits are monthly or annual; we can do a 3-6 month pilot as well. The pricing differs for short pilots but we can structure a pilot with a smaller reserved pool.
[04:45] Sasha: Do you provide tooling to estimate real-world latency after batching? We worry the batching window will push us over our 200ms p95 target.
[04:53] Samira Chen: Yes — we have a latency model and can run a micro-benchmark with your traffic to tune max batch window and concurrency. For market-sensitive flows, we usually set strict max latency and rely more on KV caching and smaller batches during peak. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 in the pilot.
[05:09] Tom Nguyen: Ok, action-wise: we want a cost model that shows per-token and per-month cost for 100k/200k/400k scenarios and a proposal for a 2-week dedicated pilot.
[05:19] Ari Kaplan: We'll produce that. Quick question: what SLA/uptime and security certifications are you expecting?
[05:25] Tom Nguyen: SOC 2 Type II is a must; ISO would be nice. Also need SSO/SAML integration and RBAC.
[05:33] Ari Kaplan: Redwood has SOC 2; ISO in progress. We support SAML/SSO, RBAC and can provide audit logs for Hosted enterprise customers. Private gives you the full network isolation if needed.
[05:45] Priya Shah: If we do Private, what's the ops burden? How long to deploy?
[05:50] Samira Chen: Private in VPC mode is typically 4-6 weeks with network setup and key management; on-prem is longer. We provide orchestration and a customer control plane; still, there's more ops overhead and a one-time integration cost.
[06:03] Liam O'Connor: For our legal team, we also need data residency in US only. Do you support region pinning?
[06:08] Ari Kaplan: Yes, both Hosted (in our US region) and Dedicated can be region-pinned. Private obviously gives you full control.
[06:15] Sasha: Slight tangent — what about model variants for cost savings, like smaller models for certain assistant intents?
[06:21] Samira Chen: Great point. Smart routing lets you route specific intents to smaller/cheaper model variants. That's a big unit-cost lever — route high-frequency simple queries to a small model and complex queries to a large one. That can cut average cost substantially.
[06:35] Tom Nguyen: That will complicate evaluation, but sounds promising. For the pilot, we want to test model multiplexing.
[06:40] Ari Kaplan: We can set up A/B rules and routing policies in the pilot.
[06:44] Priya Shah: On the pilot size — you said earlier caching can give 40% reductions; can we conservatively model 25% for initial estimates?
[06:51] Samira Chen: Conservative is good. We'll include scenarios at 15/25/40% cache hit assumptions.
[06:58] Liam O'Connor: For the benchmark, what data do you need?
[07:02] Samira Chen: Sample traffic traces (anonymized), typical session length, distribution of prompt lengths, and example prompt templates. Also expected concurrency during market hours.
[07:12] Tom Nguyen: We'll prepare that.
[07:15] Ari Kaplan: Great. Any other constraints?
[07:18] Priya Shah: Timeline: if pilot goes well, we want to go live in Q3 with Dedicated. So vendor selection decision end of April ideally.
[07:27] Ari Kaplan: That aligns. We'll expedite the pricing and pilot proposal this week.
[07:31] Sasha: A quick note — legal will want to see DPA and data handling.
[07:35] Ari Kaplan: We'll attach our standard DPA and security pack with SOC2 report.
[07:39] Tom Nguyen: Perfect.
[07:41] (brief cross-talk)
[07:45] Samira Chen: To summarize technical ask: run a 2-week Dedicated pilot sized for 100k tokens/day baseline with burst to 400k, instrument cache hit rates, measure latency with strict max batch windows, and test model multiplexing.
[08:02] Ari Kaplan: Commercial ask: draft pricing scenarios for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Dedicated+cache and a pilot quote for 2 weeks.
[08:12] Tom Nguyen: Sounds good.
[08:14] Priya Shah: One last thing — what's the onboarding support like during pilot?
[08:18] Ari Kaplan: You'll get a Solutions Eng dedicated during pilot plus an onboarding checklist, periodic syncs, and access to our benchmark tools.
[08:26] Liam O'Connor: Ok I'll send the logs and traffic profile by end of week.
[08:30] Ari Kaplan: Thanks Liam. We'll follow up with the pricing sheet and schedule the deep-dive.
[08:35] Tom Nguyen: Thanks all.

Recap (auto-summary):
- Main focus: quantify per-token economics and tradeoffs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Levers discussed: batching windows, KV/prefix caching, quantization, model multiplexing, commit sizing and burst pools.
- Next steps: Redwood to send pricing scenarios and pilot proposal; Meridian to provide traffic profile and security requirements.

End of call.
